data.narrative:
Epoch Biodesign is a Series A-stage biotech company that has raised $40M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in the Biotech & Health sector, including companies such as Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Given data constraints, only the stage-progression method is applicable. Using total capital raised ($40M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to the subsequent funding round yields an implied valuation of $80M. Public comparables in the sector trade at a median P/S of 5.5x across three tickers, but cannot be applied without Epoch's revenue figure—a data point private companies rarely disclose. A peer-median approach proved infeasible; while 8 same-sector peers exist, filtering for stage, proximity, and valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints, making a narrow comp set unreliable.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $68M (low) to $92M (high), with a median of $80M. This range reflects reasonable variance around the stage-progression anchor but carries meaningful uncertainty. The primary limitations are reliance on a single applicable method and absence of revenue data to anchor public multiples. Validation would benefit from disclosed financial metrics or a larger peer set at identical or adjacent stages.
